The use of 37 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 38 not required. 39

candidates.statement: • Exposure-response relationships should be explored during early phases of drug 132 development to aid in selection of optimal dosing strategies for evaluations in the later 133 trials. Evaluation of the relationship between drug concentration and parasite clearance 134 by integrating the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic information from in vitro and in 135 vivo drug evaluations is recommended to develop dosing strategies that avoid the 136 emergence of resistance to the investigational drug. During early phases of clinical 137 development, a simplified analysis relating exposure and proportion of participants with 138 clinical failure can be used to support evidence of effectiveness and justify dose selection. 139 Additional analyses of the exposure-safety relationship using similar approaches should 140 be performed to assist in evaluating the balance between effectiveness and toxicity of 141 different dosage regimens. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling integrated 142 with pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic information from in vitro and in vivo 143 evaluations can be useful to define dosing strategies for phase 3 development. 144 Evaluations of specific patient populations with different intrinsic factors (e.g., age, body 145 weight, and hepatic or renal impairment) in phase 3 efficacy trials can provide additional 146 information about exposure-response relationships. 147

candidates.statement: — In trials of drugs that target the erythrocytic stage parasites of Plasmodium 313 species , the primary efficacy endpoint of clinical cure is typically defined as the 314 absence of parasitemia on day 28 in participants who did not previously meet any of 315 the criteria for early treatment failure, late clinical failure, or late parasitological 316 failure. Therefore, recurrence of parasitemia after initial clearance or persistence of 317 parasitemia during the 28-day period would be considered a failure. Duplicate blood 318 smears should be examined frequently, for example, every 6 to 12 hours until 319 parasitemia has been eradicated; eradication is defined as two successive parasite- 320 negative smears. If parasitological eradication has occurred, subsequent malaria 321 smears should be examined at least once a week until the end of the study on day 28. 322

candidates.statement:  Differences in Plasmodium parasite genotyping methods can affect estimates of 355 corrected cure rates in clinical trials across different epidemiological settings. It 356 is recommended that the performance of the genotyping assay(s) be assessed 357 across different geographic regions with a range of transmission intensities (e.g., 358 low, moderate, and high), multiplicity of infection (e.g., variation in the 359 prevalence and number of genetically distinct dominant and minority/low-density 360 parasite clones/strains) and allelic frequencies; such information will be useful in 361 understanding the epidemiological settings and the diversity of genotyping 362 markers in the study population. The validity of the genotype results depends on 363 systematic analysis of the test performance including but not limited to sensitivity, 364 specificity, and reproducibility, as well as effective quality control assessments. 365 The details of the methods used, the performance characteristics of the assays, and 366 quality control parameters implemented in the laboratory where testing of clinical 367 specimens will be conducted should be well documented. The performance of the 368 laboratory should be in accordance with Clinical Laboratory Improvement 369 Amendments. The data elements to be collected should be discussed with the 370 Agency. 371

candidates.statement: — Modified intent-to-treat population : All randomized participants with a 463 microbiologically confirmed Plasmodium species at baseline. For both noninferiority 464 and superiority trials the primary efficacy assessment is typically conducted on a 465 modified intent-to-treat analysis population. In noninferiority trials the modified 466 intent-to-treat population should exclude participants if the control is not effective 467 against the baseline pathogen(s). In superiority trials the modified intent-to-treat 468 population may or may not exclude participants based on the activity of the control 469 against the baseline pathogen(s). Participants should not be excluded from this 470 population based on events that occur after randomization (e.g., lost to follow-up). 471

candidates.statement: • New infections should be considered treatment failures in the primary efficacy analyses 476 for the following reasons: Firstly, from a patient perspective, any new infection is a 477 failure. Secondly, there is a possibility that the new Plasmodium strain was present in 478 low density at baseline. Lastly, a new infection requires treatment, thus confounding an 479 assessment of relapse/recrudescence. Additional analyses separating failures by 480 relapse/recrudescence and new infection should be conducted. 481
